Ransomware Attack Disrupts Spanish Hospitality Sector Operations

A major ransomware incident is causing widespread disruption across Spain’s hospitality industry, with hotels and restaurants in multiple regions reporting severe IT outages. The attack, which began early Tuesday morning, has forced several leading hospitality groups, including Grupo Solera and the hotel chain Costa Urbana, to take key booking and management systems offline as a precaution.

Front desk and reservations staff at affected establishments are struggling to process check-ins and manage guest services, as digital systems for room allocation, payment processing, and housekeeping coordination remain inaccessible. Many guests have reported delays at check-in and difficulties accessing their rooms, with some hotels resorting to manual registration and handwritten room keys.

“The situation is very challenging,” said Elena Martínez, spokesperson for the Spanish Hospitality Association. “Our member firms are working around the clock to restore services, but the impact on both operations and customer experience is significant. Staff are doing their best, but without access to our usual IT tools, everything takes longer.”

In several cities, hospitality workers’ unions are expressing concern for employees now working overtime to manage the backlog. “Our members are under enormous stress,” said Juan Delgado, regional leader of the Federación de Trabajadores de Hostelería. “They’re dealing with frustrated guests while also having to improvise solutions with pen and paper.”

Security analysts believe the ransomware was introduced via a phishing email targeting central administration offices of major hospitality groups. While no ransom amount has been disclosed, a statement from Grupo Solera confirmed that attackers are demanding payment in cryptocurrency to decrypt business-critical files.

Restaurants operated by the affected groups have also been hit. Point-of-sale terminals are down, forcing many locations to switch to cash-only transactions or close temporarily. “We have closed three sites in Madrid today because we simply can’t process orders,” said Luis Herrera, operations manager for Costa Urbana’s restaurant division.

The Spanish Hospitality Association has called for urgent government support, including cybersecurity assistance and guidance on mitigating further risks. As of Wednesday evening, there is no clear timeline for restoration of normal service, with several industry bodies warning that disruptions may extend into the weekend.
